doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: Billie first notices De De and tells Sadie she likes him
summary: Billie tells how she saw De De, Sadie's trumpet player, told Sadie she liked him, and finally told him herself walking home after work on Decatur Street.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, well, I thought I was going to say, I didn't know though he was in the Florida band. Yeah, yeah. I was going to say, it sure looks like D.D. I'm going to roll. Yeah, I'm going to roll. I'm going to roll. I didn't know what's wrong. He holds the horn like he does, and everything looks like D.D. When did you all get, I mean, I know when you got married, but when did you, how did you meet? I was going to ask about that. Influence, I was working with her sister Sadie.
Let me tell him how I met you. Let me tell him, because he ain't going to tell you that I got told you.

Maybe each one of you got a different story on that. Now, this is the case though. Well, see, when my sister went here Sadie, I was staying with Sadie, I was working around with Lawrence Togel and the different bands going around, you know, just wild, understand? Yeah. Just having my fun. And, I don't know, so I never did see the trouble. I might have seen him, but I wasn't paying no attention, really. I might have been in different places, you know, like we used to go out to what we call those speakeasers and things like that, you understand? I might have met him, might have been drinking with him before, I know of, you know, but I didn't know him personally, see? So finally one day Sadie was home, I was there, and D.D. came home. So I said to my sister, I just said, I just walked through and in, says hello, he says hello, and I'll come on, I'll go on again, see? That's all I have to say. So, when I came back home that evening, whenever they get back, I asked my sister, I says, Sadie, she said, huh? I said, who's that little fellow, just like that, who's that little fellow? She said, that's my trumpet player, trumpet player, I said, what's his name? Diddy, I said, Diddy, yeah? I said, huh, just like that. She said, did you know there's something I was going to say, you know? She said, what I was going to say? I said, that's your boyfriend? She said, no, that ain't no my boyfriend. She said, why you asked me something like that? I said, cause if it ain't your boyfriend, tell him I like the hell out of him. So, he said, listen, let me tell you one thing, say, nah, listen, Billy, I know you. He said, D.D. is a nice boy and everything, and Billy, I don't, you, I see for yourself, you don't mean no, no one man no good. I said, if I don't mean no one man no good, I sure hell mean him some good. Just like that.
